proposal_summary.method: Hebrew discourse, quoted objections, address and command shifts, rhetorical results, and correlated paragraph evidence; larger coherent disputations prevail when a child cannot preserve accusation-answer-consequence logic alone.

source_pins.use: pointed Hebrew, morphology locators, paragraph marks

rules.rule: WEB chapter 4 verse n maps to MT/WLC chapter 3 verse n+18

translation_hot_zones.pressure: מַלְאָכִי and messenger/name relation; no name, office, or authorship decision.
אהב and שנא contrast exceeds an English gloss; roots do not decide relation or theology.
Tense/aspect, offering, table-food, weariness, sniffing, and seized-animal wording remain inside the dispute.
גֶּרַע offspring/seed and rebuke syntax do not create a seam.
Father/creator referents, foreign-god idiom, and עֵר וְעֹנֶה are unresolved.
One/residue/spirit/offspring and hate/send/divorce/garment/violence syntax are unresolved; repeated treachery frames the unit.
Two messenger expressions and speaker shifts are retained without identity or fulfillment selection.
עַד־בְּלִי־דָי sufficiency/limit pressure does not split command from promise.
Memory-book, treasured-possession, and day-I-make language support the response scene without doctrinal selection.
Sun-of-righteousness and healing-wings images receive no external identity.
Reciprocal kinship and חֵרֶם remain in the coda without legal or eschatological ruling.

route.title: Oracle heading hydrated with the love-and-Edom disputation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: מַשָּׂא דְבַר־יְהוָה governs the speech; 1:2 begins אָהַבְתִּי ... וַאֲמַרְתֶּם בַּמָּה, 1:5 closes with seeing and saying, and 1:6 shifts to a son-servant analogy plus explicit priestly vocative.
route.rationale: The first objection supplies the heading's complete claim-counterclaim-demonstration-result movement. Edom's rebuild counterclaim and reversal culminate in 1:5 recognition, while לָכֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים at 1:6 changes addressee and accusation.

rejected_alternatives.reason: A title-only surface lacks the governed utterance and invites name/messenger proof-texting.
Valid dependent child, but without 1:1 it loses the oracle frame.

counterevidence: Mal.1.1 is a superscription distinct from direct speech in 1:2.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.1.1 מַשָּׂא דְבַר יְהוָה ... בְּיַד מַלְאָכִי
OSHB Mal.1.5 וְעֵינֵיכֶם תִּרְאֶינָה וְאַתֶּם תֹּאמְרוּ

internal_seams.basis: Direct speech begins after the superscription, but its first dispute remains hydrated.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate מַלְאָכִי to decide personal name, office, messenger identity, or authorship; keep the Jacob-Esau contrast inside the love objection and recognition close.

route.title: Priestly honor and polluted-offering disputation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: The priestly vocative and בַּמֶּה objection at 1:6 open the charge; renewed objections, defective offerings, governor comparison, rejection, nations contrast, and וְאָרוּר נוֹכֵל ... כִּי מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל אָנִי carry it to curse and rationale.
route.rationale: Verses 1:6-9 establish despised name and polluted altar. Verse 1:10 pivots to temple-door wish and worldwide-name contrast; 1:12-13 turns that contrast against the priests, and 1:14 supplies the deceiver curse and great-name reason. The samekh after 1:13 is genuine counterevidence, so the larger unit is retained but treatment is held.

rejected_alternatives.reason: The second panel resumes the polluted-table accusation; both children require the whole dispute.
The samekh supports presentation separation, but standalone 1:14 loses the sacrificial deceit and functions as the dispute's curse coda.

counterevidence: OSHB and UXLC place samekh after Mal.1.13.
Mal.1.10 is a marked wish-rejection-nations turn.
Mal.1.14 follows the marker but echoes 1:11's great-name rationale.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.1.6 לָכֶם הַכֹּהֲנִים ... וַאֲמַרְתֶּם בַּמֶּה
OSHB Mal.1.10 מִי גַם בָּכֶם וְיִסְגֹּר דְּלָתַיִם
OSHB Mal.1.14 וְאָרוּר נוֹכֵל ... כִּי מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל אָנִי
route.hold_question: Should the primary surface remain Mal.1.6-1.14 as the complete disputation, or should the samekh authorize dependent Mal.1.6-1.13 and Mal.1.14 surfaces with mandatory Mal.1.6-1.14 hydration? The former preserves accusation-to-curse logic; the latter preserves textual presentation without making 1:14 an independent proof text.

mandatory_parent.reason: Offering accusation and ensuing priestly command are address-linked movements of a larger indictment.

internal_seams.basis: Door-closing wish starts rejection and nations contrast.
Correlated samekh precedes a semantically necessary curse coda.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not detach 1:11 to decide tense, worship geography, or offering practice; do not detach 1:14 from the defective-offering accusation.

route.title: Command to the priests and covenant-of-Levi indictment
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: וְעַתָּה אֲלֵיכֶם הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת הַכֹּהֲנִים restarts at 2:1; 2:4 names covenant purpose, 2:5-7 gives Levi's ideal, וְאַתֶּם at 2:8 contrasts failure, and a pe after 2:9 closes consequence.
route.rationale: Threatened curse establishes why the command was sent concerning Levi. The ideal mouth/path/messenger panel is the comparison for adversative priestly failure and public consequence. The explicit command onset and pe define a child distinct from the offering dispute while the larger priestly parent remains mandatory.

rejected_alternatives.reason: The command states the covenant with Levi as its purpose, so the comparison cannot be detached.
Ideal and failure are joined by וְאַתֶּם and require comparison.
Coherent mandatory parent, but the explicit 2:1 command justifies a retrievable child.

counterevidence: The priestly addressee continues from 1:6.
Mal.2.5 and 2:8 mark useful dependent panels.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.2.1 וְעַתָּה אֲלֵיכֶם הַמִּצְוָה הַזֹּאת הַכֹּהֲנִים
OSHB Mal.2.4 לִהְיוֹת בְּרִיתִי אֶת לֵוִי

mandatory_parent.reason: Hydration preserves the full priestly indictment across the explicit restart.

internal_seams.basis: וְאַתֶּם turns to present failure and sentence.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate Mal.2.7's priest-as-messenger line to settle office, authority, or covenant theology.

route.title: Communal brother-treachery and foreign-god accusation
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: First-person-plural הֲלוֹא ... לְכֻלָּנוּ and מַדּוּעַ נִבְגַּד change voice and scope at 2:10; judgment ends at a pe after 2:12 before וְזֹאת שֵׁנִית in 2:13.
route.rationale: Shared-father and creator questions frame Judah's profanation as one communal accusation, and 2:12 supplies consequence. The pe plus explicit second-act formula makes 2:10-12 a real child while hydration preserves the whole treachery complex.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Questions announce but do not state conduct or consequence.
Mandatory parent, but pe plus 'this second' supports two children.

counterevidence: Repeated בגד links 2:10-12 and 2:13-16.
Father/creator referents and עֵר וְעֹנֶה are translation hot zones.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.2.10 הֲלוֹא אָב אֶחָד לְכֻלָּנוּ ... מַדּוּעַ נִבְגַּד

mandatory_parent.reason: Repeated treachery and 'second' make both accusations children of one parent.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not use one-father, one-God, foreign-god, or paired-expression wording to decide referents, marriage law, exclusion, or ritual status.

route.title: Second treachery accusation concerning the wife of youth
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: וְזֹאת שֵׁנִית תַּעֲשׂוּ opens a second act after pe; וַאֲמַרְתֶּם עַל־מָה gives the objection, repeated בגד and נשמרתם bind answer and warning, and samekh after 2:16 closes.
route.rationale: Altar tears pose the consequence, 'why?' introduces Yahweh's covenant witness, and compressed 2:15-16 repeats guard-your-spirit and treachery language. Syntax is difficult, but the explicit onset and closing marker define the outer unit without deciding translation or law.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Witness explanation continues into repeated spirit-guard and treachery commands; difficulty is not a seam.
Cannot stand as a law proof-text apart from altar complaint and covenant-witness answer.
Parent remains mandatory, while pe and 'second' support this child.

counterevidence: Mal.2.15-16 has severe clause, subject, and translation ambiguity.
Covenant and treachery language links backward.

mandatory_parent.reason: The second accusation presupposes the first and shares treachery vocabulary.

internal_seams.basis: Compressed syntax begins, but repeated spirit-guard and treachery sustain continuity.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not surface 2:15-16 alone to decide Spirit, offspring, monogamy, marriage, divorce, hate, violence, or law.

route.title: Justice complaint answered by messenger, refining, and judgment
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: 2:17 opens הוֹגַעְתֶּם ... וַאֲמַרְתֶּם and asks אַיֵּה אֱלֹהֵי הַמִּשְׁפָּט; 3:1 answers הִנְנִי שֹׁלֵחַ מַלְאָכִי, 3:2 tests endurance, and 3:5 returns to לַמִּשְׁפָּט as swift witness.
route.rationale: The WEB chapter edge falls between complaint and answer. Way-preparation, coming, endurance, refining, restored offerings, and judgment resolve the claims that evil is pleasing and justice absent; 3:6 then begins a new first-person grounding and return dispute.

rejected_alternatives.reason: The justice question is the antecedent answered by coming and judgment; no source marker supports the chapter split.
Messenger line lacks complaint, endurance, refining result, and judgment.
Swift witness is the judicial outcome and repeats מִשְׁפָּט.

counterevidence: Mal.3.1 has strong הִנְנִי onset as an answer child.
Messenger, Lord, covenant-messenger, and first-person references complicate translation.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.3.2 וּמִי מְכַלְכֵּל ... וּמִי הָעֹמֵד

internal_seams.basis: הִנְנִי begins the answer but resolves 2:17.
Swift witness gives the answer's result.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 3:1 to select messenger/speaker identity, fulfillment, chronology, or temple theology; later reuse is not boundary authority.

route.title: Return summons made concrete in the tithe dispute
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה לֹא שָׁנִיתִי grounds 3:6; שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי and בַּמֶּה נָשׁוּב lead to the 3:8 robbery objection, הָבִיאוּ and וּבְחָנוּנִי supply remedy, and nations coda ends at samekh after 3:12.
route.rationale: The broad return summons asks how to return, and the tithe accusation answers with wrong, command, test, crop protection, and nations recognition. Splitting at 3:8 leaves the objection unanswered; splitting after the imperative loses promised result.

rejected_alternatives.reason: The concrete accusation answers בַּמֶּה נָשׁוּב; both require the parent.
Command and test do not complete the promise until 3:11-12.

counterevidence: Mal.3.8 begins a fresh question and objection as a dependent child.
Mal.3.6 may bridge backward as well as ground the return dispute.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.3.6 כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה לֹא שָׁנִיתִי
OSHB Mal.3.7 שׁוּבוּ אֵלַי ... בַּמֶּה נָשׁוּב

internal_seams.basis: New robbery question directly answers 3:7's return objection.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate 3:10 to settle obligation, testing practice, prosperity claims, or עַד־בְּלִי־דָי.

route.title: Harsh-words protest answered by the fearers' counter-scene
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: חָזְקוּ עָלַי דִּבְרֵיכֶם and וַאֲמַרְתֶּם open at 3:13; אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי יְהוָה turns to an answering group in 3:16, and 3:18 closes with servant/non-servant discernment before samekh.
route.rationale: The claim that service is futile is answered narratively: fearers speak, Yahweh hears, a record is written, and possession and sparing lead to discernment between the same service categories. The 3:16 response is a child, but it is the accusation's lexical and rhetorical answer.

rejected_alternatives.reason: The response scene is the direct counterexample to service-is-futile speech.
Mandatory parent preserves the day contrast, while samekh after 3:18 and pe after 4:3 support two children.

counterevidence: אָז at 3:16 changes actors.
Samekh after 3:18 marks presentation break.
כִּי הִנֵּה at 4:1 makes the next child causally dependent.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.3.13 חָזְקוּ עָלַי דִּבְרֵיכֶם ... וַאֲמַרְתֶּם
OSHB Mal.3.16 אָז נִדְבְּרוּ יִרְאֵי יְהוָה ... וַיִּכָּתֵב סֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן
OSHB Mal.3.18 בֵּין עֹבֵד אֱלֹהִים לַאֲשֶׁר לֹא עֲבָדוֹ

mandatory_parent.reason: The coming-day contrast explains promised discernment and completes servant/wicked argument.

internal_seams.basis: אָז changes actors, but the scene answers the protest.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate memory book or treasured possession to decide election, salvation, reward, or chronology.

route.title: Coming-day contrast for the wicked and name-fearers
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: WEB 4:1 is MT/WLC 3:19 and begins כִּי הִנֵּה הַיּוֹם בָּא after samekh; three verses contrast wrongdoers and name-fearers and close at pe after MT/WLC 3:21 before זִכְרוּ.
route.rationale: Causal כִּי links the day oracle to 3:18 discernment, so it is not an independent fragment. Yet samekh before, complete burning/healing contrast, and pe after WEB 4:3 justify a dependent surface with mandatory 3:13-4:3 hydration.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Treading and ashes complete the contrast and close at pe.
Wicked and fearer panels are a deliberate comparison.
Parent remains mandatory; paragraph marks support the child day oracle.

counterevidence: Initial כִּי makes 4:1 dependent on 3:18.
WEB chapter division has no independent Hebrew authority; this is MT/WLC 3:19-21.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.3.19 כִּי הִנֵּה הַיּוֹם בָּא

mandatory_parent.reason: The כִּי day explanation completes protest, fearers, discernment, and judgment contrast.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not isolate sun-of-righteousness, healing wings, root/branch, or treading images to select identity, fulfillment, chronology, or violence.

route.title: Moses remembrance and Elijah sending coda
route.deciding_marker_or_seam: After pe at MT/WLC 3:21, זִכְרוּ תּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה commands remembrance; הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ begins the paired sending, and 4:6 supplies reconciliation purpose and פֶּן ... חֵרֶם risk.
route.rationale: The coda pairs what Israel must remember with what the speaker will send before the day. Reciprocal heart-turning and the lest-clause are purpose and risk, so neither panel surfaces alone. The preceding pe and new commands distinguish the coda without granting WEB chapter authority.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Command and promise are paired as one closing frame; children require the whole coda.
Heart-turning and curse-risk state sending's purpose and consequence.
Final חֵרֶם clause is not a standalone curse unit.

counterevidence: זִכְרוּ and הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ introduce distinguishable child panels.
Named figures prompt later reuse, but reuse is not local splitting authority.
evidence_refs: OSHB Mal.3.23 הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי שֹׁלֵחַ ... אֵלִיָּה
OSHB Mal.3.24 וְהֵשִׁיב לֵב ... פֶּן ... חֵרֶם

internal_seams.basis: Sending formula remains paired with remembrance command and purpose close.

route.proof_text_guard: Do not separate Moses, Elijah, heart-turning, or חֵרֶם to decide identity, fulfillment, order, family law, eschatology, or curse authority.

independence_declaration.statement: Derived independently from pinned strategy, Malachi WEB rows, and two correlated WLC-family views. OSHB/UXLC agreement is not independent-witness or cross-model convergence.

limits: No boundary is reviewed gold or canonical authority.
Paragraph marks, accents, morphology, lemmas, and roots are evidence only.
No name, authorship, messenger identity, priestly authority, marriage/divorce law, covenant system, fulfillment, eschatology, theology, chronology, or preferred witness is decided.
Later canonical reuse is not local boundary authority.
